```{r}
#Libraries being used
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(devtools)
library(lme4)
library(effects)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(tidyr)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(interactions)
require(car)
library(reshape2)
```

```{r}
## read in full data set for awareness part
full_data<- read.csv("full_data_osf.csv")
```

```{r}
## change the format of the full data set
#wide to long prep, so each pt has 2 starting points and 4 social identities. 

full.long<- melt(data = full_data, measure.vars = c("disability_no_low_to_mid", 
                                                  "disability_sensory_low_to_mid",
                                                  "disability_physical_low_to_mid",
                                                  "disability_learning_low_to_mid",
                                                  "disability_no_mid_to_high", 
                                                  "disability_physical_mid_to_high",
                                                  "disability_sensory_mid_to_high",
                                                  "disability_learning_mid_to_high"
                                                   ),
                      variable.name = "ses_identity",
                      value.name = "likelihood_of_sm")

full.long<-mutate(full.long, starting = case_when(
  ses_identity == "disability_no_low_to_mid" ~ 'low', 
  ses_identity == "disability_sensory_low_to_mid"~ 'low',
  ses_identity == "disability_physical_low_to_mid" ~'low', 
  ses_identity == "disability_learning_low_to_mid" ~ 'low', 
  ses_identity == "disability_physical_mid_to_high" ~ 'mid', 
  ses_identity == "disability_no_mid_to_high"~ 'mid',
  ses_identity == "disability_sensory_mid_to_high" ~'mid', 
  ses_identity == "disability_learning_mid_to_high" ~ 'mid'))


full.long<-mutate(full.long, category = case_when(
  ses_identity == "disability_no_low_to_mid" ~ 'no_disability', 
  ses_identity == "disability_no_mid_to_high" ~ 'no_disability', 
  ses_identity == "disability_sensory_low_to_mid" ~ 'sensory', 
  ses_identity == "disability_sensory_mid_to_high" ~ 'sensory', 
  ses_identity == "disability_physical_low_to_mid" ~ 'physical', 
  ses_identity == "disability_physical_mid_to_high" ~ 'physical', 
  ses_identity == "disability_learning_low_to_mid" ~ 'learning', 
  ses_identity == "disability_learning_mid_to_high" ~ 'learning'))

## change the reference groups and structure of data
full.long$sid =factor(full.long$sid)
full.long$culture<- factor(full.long$culture, levels = c("US", "Chinese"))
full.long$starting<- factor(full.long$starting, levels = c("mid", "low"))
full.long$category<- factor(full.long$category, levels = c("no_disability", "sensory", "physical", "learning"))
full.long$version <- factor(full.long$version, levels = c("1","2","3","4"))
full.long$age_group<- factor(full.long$age_group, levels = c("adult", "child"))
full.long$location <- factor(full.long$location, levels = c("online", "in person"))
full.long$gender <- factor(full.long$gender, levels = c("female", "male", "nonbinary"))
#n = 2840 because 355*8 = 2840
```

```{r}
## checking models

## order
checking_model_order = lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ version*category + (1|sid), data = full.long)
summary(checking_model_order)  ## no effect of order, so we will not consider it in all subsequent models

## gender
checking_model_gender = lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ gender*category + (1|sid), data = full.long)
summary(checking_model_gender)  ## a main effect of gender, so we will include it as a random effect across all models

## location (only in child data)
checking_model_location = lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ location*category + (1|sid), data = subset(full.long, age_group == "child"))
summary(checking_model_location)  ## no effect of location, so we will not include it in all subsequent models
```

```{r}
## Do participants express awareness of disability-based disparities in upward mobility, and does this change across development? We answered this question by running a comprehensive model with data from all participants.
comprehensive_model<- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture*age_group*category*starting+ (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = full.long)
summary(comprehensive_model)
```

```{r}
## Confirmatory Analyses

## Do children and adults in the U.S. express an awareness of disparities in upward mobility based on disability status, and does this awareness change across development?

## Analyses for U.S. children and adults 
us.long <- subset(full.long, culture =="US")

## Do U.S. participants express awareness of disability-based disparities in upward mobility?
us_model_full <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_group*starting + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = us.long)
summary(us_model_full) # no 3-way interaction, so drop starting as the predictor for graph
us_model_full_2<- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_group+ (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = us.long)
summary(us_model_full_2)
```

```{r}
## descriptive numbers calculation
## calculate the mean and SD of for children and adults separately
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ age_group, data = us.long, FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ age_group, data = us.long, FUN = sd)

## calculate the mean and SD for each disability category 
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = us.long, FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = us.long, FUN = sd)

## calculate the mean and SD for each category among U.S. adults
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(us.long, age_group == "adult"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(us.long, age_group == "adult"), FUN = sd)

## calculate the mean and SD for each category among U.S. children
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(us.long, age_group == "child"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(us.long, age_group == "child"), FUN = sd)

```

```{r}
## post-hoc analysis: U.S. children vs. U.S. adults 
US_pairwise <- emmeans(us_model_full, pairwise ~ age_group*category)
US_pairwise <-as.data.frame(US_pairwise)
US_pairwise 
write.csv(US_pairwise, "US_pairwise.csv")

emm_US_mean<- effect("category*age_group", us_model_full_2, confidence.level = 0.95)
emm_US_mean <-as.data.frame(emm_US_mean)
emm_US_mean
view(emm_US_mean)
```


```{r}
## Figure 1

## re-level the data so the categories on x-axis follow a certain order
emm_US_mean$category <- factor(emm_US_mean$category,
                              levels = c("no_disability", "physical", "sensory", "learning"))
us.long$category <- factor(us.long$category,
                           levels = c("no_disability", "physical", "sensory", "learning"))

## graph the Chinese data: children and adults: lower status

Figure_1<-ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = emm_US_mean, 
             aes(x = category, y = fit, colour = age_group), 
             stat = "identity", size = 2) +
    geom_jitter(data = us.long,
              aes(x = category, y = likelihood_of_sm, colour = age_group),
              stat = "identity", size = 0.5, alpha = .50, height = 0, width = 0.25, shape = 124) + ylim(1,5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = emm_US_mean,
                width = .2,
                aes(x = category, ymax = upper, ymin = lower, colour = age_group)) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks=c("no_disability", "physical", "sensory", "learning"), labels = c("No disability","Physical disability", "Sensory disability", "Learning disability")) + 
  theme_few() +
  theme(axis.text=element_text(size=10),
        axis.title=element_text(size=10)) +
  scale_colour_solarized() +
  labs(y = "Likelihood of upward social mobility", x = "Disability status", color = "age group")

Figure_1
  
Figure_1 <- ggsave("Figure_1.tiff", units="in", width=7, height=6, dpi=700, compression = 'lzw')

```



```{r}
##Analyses for U.S. children
us.child.long = subset(us.long, age_group =="child")
## center the age
summary(us.child.long$age_exact)  ## get the averaged age = 7.03
us.child.long $ age_centered = us.child.long $ age_exact -  7.03

## MAIN MODEL
# Do U.S.children express awareness of disparities in upward mobility for families with different disability status?
us_child_model <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ starting*category*age_centered + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = us.child.long)
summary(us_child_model)

## post-hoc analysis
## separate the data into 2 models: one for economically advantaged families, one for economically disadvantaged families
## model for economically disadvantaged families
us.child.long.low = subset(us.child.long, starting == "low")
us_child_model_low <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_centered + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = us.child.long.low)
summary(us_child_model_low)

## model for economically disadvantaged families
us.child.long.high = subset(us.child.long, starting == "mid")
us_child_model_high <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_centered + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = us.child.long.high)
summary(us_child_model_high)
```

```{r}
## Age-related changes in U.S. children
## economically disadvantaged families
slope<-sim_slopes(model = us_child_model_low, pred = age_centered, modx = category)
slope$slope
## significant for sensory disability: with age, U.S. children were less likely to expect social mobility for economically advantaged families with a sensory disability

## economically advantaged families
slope<-sim_slopes(model = us_child_model_high, pred = age_centered, modx = category)
slope$slope
## significant for families with no disability: with age, U.S. children were more likely to expect social mobility for economically advantaged families with no disability.
## significant for families with a physical disability: with age, U.S. children were less likely to expect social mobility for economically advantaged families with a physical disability.
```

```{r}
## Do children and adults in China express an awareness of disparities in upward mobility based on disability status, and does this awareness change across development? 

## Analyses for Chinese children and adults 
chinese.long = subset(full.long, culture =="Chinese")

## pre-registered model
chinese_model_full <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_group*starting + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = chinese.long)
summary(chinese_model_full) 

## separate the Chinese data by starting point of the families
chinese.long.low = subset(chinese.long, starting == "low")
chinese.long.high= subset(chinese.long, starting == "mid")

## run separate models for data of families with each starting point
chinese_model_full_low <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_group + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = chinese.long.low)
summary(chinese_model_full_low)

chinese_model_full_high <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ category*age_group + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = chinese.long.high)
summary(chinese_model_full_high)

## calculate the mean and sd for each category (by starting point)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.low, age_group == "adult"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.low, age_group == "adult"), FUN = sd)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.low, age_group == "child"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.low, age_group == "child"), FUN = sd)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.high, age_group == "adult"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.high, age_group == "adult"), FUN = sd)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.high, age_group == "child"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ category, data = subset(chinese.long.high, age_group == "child"), FUN = sd)
```

```{r}
## Exploratory Analyses
## Does culture moderate adults’ awareness of disparities in upward social mobility by disability status?

## pool adult data from the U.S. and China
adult.long = subset(full.long, age_group == "adult")
adult_model_culture <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ starting*category*culture + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = adult.long)
summary(adult_model_culture)
## interaction involving culture and starting point

## post-hoc analyses
emm_adult <- emmeans(adult_model_culture, pairwise ~ starting*culture)
emm_adult
emm_pairwise_adult <- emmeans(adult_model_culture, pairwise ~ starting*culture)
emm_pairwise_adult <-as.data.frame(emm_pairwise_adult)
emm_pairwise_adult

## calculate the mean and sd for adults in each culture
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = adult.long, FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = adult.long, FUN = sd)

aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = subset(adult.long, starting == "low"), FUN = mean)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = subset(adult.long, starting == "mid"), FUN = mean)

aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = subset(adult.long, starting == "low"), FUN = sd)
aggregate(likelihood_of_sm ~ culture, data = subset(adult.long, starting == "mid"), FUN = sd)

## pool child data from the U.S. and China
child.long = subset(full.long, age_group == "child")
child_model_culture <- lmer(likelihood_of_sm ~ starting*category*culture + (1|sid) + (1|gender), data = child.long)
summary(child_model_culture)
## no effect involving culture
```


```{r}
## Do children’s beliefs about disparities in social mobility relate to their decision to rectify or perpetuate inequalities 

long.resource<- melt(data = full_data, measure.vars = c("disability_money_choice", 
                                                  "disability_camp_choice"),
                      variable.name = "type",
                      value.name = "choice")

long.resource$choice = as.factor(long.resource$choice)
long.resource$choice <- ifelse(long.resource$choice == "perpetuate", 0, 1)

## U.S. child data
long.resource.us.child = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "child" & long.resource$culture == "US")
## get the averaged age for the sample
summary(long.resource.us.child$age_exact)  ## get the averaged age = 7.03
## center the age
long.resource.us.child $ age_centered = long.resource.us.child $ age_exact -  7.05
resource_model_child_us = glmer(choice ~ type * age_centered + (1|sid), family = binomial, data = long.resource.us.child)
summary(resource_model_child_us)

## Chinese child data
long.resource.chinese.child = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "child" & long.resource$culture == "Chinese")
## get the averaged age for the sample
summary(long.resource.chinese.child$age_exact)  ## get the averaged age = 6.89
## center the age
long.resource.chinese.child $ age_centered = long.resource.chinese.child $ age_exact -  6.89
resource_model_child_chinese = glmer(choice ~ type * age_centered + (1|sid), family = binomial, data = long.resource.chinese.child)
summary(resource_model_child_chinese)

## pool data from Chinese and U.S. children
long.resource.child = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "child")
## get the averaged age for the sample
summary(long.resource.child$age_exact)  ## get the averaged age = 6.96
## center the age
long.resource.child $ age_centered = long.resource.child $ age_exact -  6.96
resource_model_child = glmer(choice ~ type * age_centered *culture + (1|sid), family = binomial, data = long.resource.child)
summary(resource_model_child)
```


```{r}
## Figure 5 Left
```

```{r}
## only look at Chinese child data
long.resource.chinese.child = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "child" & long.resource$culture == "Chinese")
## get the averaged age for the sample
summary(long.resource.chinese.child$age_exact)  ## get the averaged age = 6.89
## center the age
long.resource.chinese.child $ age_centered = long.resource.chinese.child $ age_exact -  6.89
resource_model_child_chinese = glmer(choice ~ type * age_centered + (1|sid), family = binomial, data = long.resource.chinese.child)
summary(resource_model_child_chinese)
```

```{r}
## Additional Analyses in SOM
## resource allocation of U.S. adults
long.resource.us.adult = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "adult" & long.resource$culture == "US")
resource_model_us_adult = lmer(choice ~ type + (1|sid), data = long.resource.us.adult)
summary(resource_model_us_adult) ## main effect of type of resource, camp<money

## money
binom.test(78,82, 0.5, alternative = "two.sided") 

## camp
binom.test(72,82, 0.5, alternative = "two.sided") 

## resource allocation of Chinese adults
long.resource.chinese.adult = subset (long.resource, long.resource$age_group == "adult" & long.resource$culture == "Chinese")
resource_model_china_adult = lmer(choice ~ type + (1|sid), data = long.resource.chinese.adult)

summary(resource_model_china_adult) ## main effect of type of resource, camp<money

## money
binom.test(97,102, 0.5, alternative = "two.sided") 

## camp
binom.test(85,102, 0.5, alternative = "two.sided") 
```











```{r}
## additional playmate questions
## library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
## us
# 1. Read data
playmate_us_long<- read.csv("playmate_us_long.csv")

# Set reference group
playmate_us_long$family_type <- relevel(
  factor(playmate_us_long$family_type),
  ref = "no_disability"
)

## mean center sm ratings
playmate_us_long <- playmate_us_long %>%
  mutate(
    mobility_rating_c = mobility_rating - mean(mobility_rating, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Run model
playmate_us <- clogit(
  choice ~ mobility_rating * family_type +
    strata(sid),
  data = playmate_us_long
)

summary(playmate_us)
```
